collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two families who have quarreled for years both lose someone in the same storm: mourn together, or mourn apart.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A storm took two fishers last week: one from (subject)'s family, one from (friend)'s. The two families have not spoken in years, over a garden boundary. The village is planning the mourning gathering, and someone has suggested holding one gathering for both. Neither family has answered. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes to (friend)'s hut and says, simply, that they should mourn together. (friend) agrees. At the gathering, the two families stand side by side and sing for their dead. Afterwards they go back to not speaking, mostly. But the next time the garden boundary comes up, nobody raises their voice.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) does not go. The two families hold separate gatherings on the same night, at either end of the beach, and the village splits between them. Some people go to both. From the middle of the beach, both songs can be heard at once.
